title: Muuyawkatsina - Moon Spirit
description: Illustration of Muuyawu, a Kachina moon spirit of the Hopi People of Southern Arizona - widely considered one of the oldest living cultures in the world. Originally by Gerald Dawavendewa (Hopi & Cherokee).
process: Started with a pencil sketch of the figure and traced over that with fine liners of different weights. Red circle made with acrylic, painted flat and left to dry. It was a joy to try and find the perfect shade by mixing and experimenting.
inspiration: Hopi culture and their Kachina dolls. I just loved the expression of the figure, reminiscent of a traveller of the nights.
meaning: Something about being watched over at night by an entity that slightly unsettles you. The figure isn't doing anything — just being present, looking into you.

title: Taawakatsina - Sun Spirit
description: My reimagination of Taawa, the sun spirit of the Hopi People regarded as the creator of the First World and a guide through existance. Often associated with fertility, life and growth.
process: Rough pencil sketch traced on with fine liners. Used different hatching techniques to create visual somplexity and depth. I chose a lush deep green to represent the sun.
inspiration: Hopi culture and their Kachina dolls. They usually have feline features and the sun spirit looked particularly playful just floating around
meaning: To me, they respresent the will of life, radiating out.

title: Madhubani_1
description: My highly simplified take on the classic Tree of Life motif seen in various artforms across the country. Representing the interconnectedness of all life. This was a gift to my fiance's grandmother so it needed extra care and patience. I tried to incorporate elements that dont usually go into this sort of imagery, like the sky or the arches.
process: Rough pencil sketch of half of the tree made on tracing paper and mirrored on the ither side to create symmetry then traced on with fine liners. Used the finest point liner to hatch and dot, somethign I greatly enjoy doing.
inspiration: Tree of life motif in Pattachitra style of Odisha. Border is a common pattern in Madhubani. The gold represents the 'fruits' of life.
meaning: It means family and beauty. Projecting our hopes into the future.
